newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, Belarus leaders meet in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Russian, Belarus leaders meet in Moscow.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin met visiting Belarus leader Alexander Lukashenko for more talks on closer union between the two Slav states, both formerly part of the Soviet Union.
Yeltsin, who looked energetic and fit, welcomed the hardline Belarus president in his Kremlin residence, saying that Moscow was committed to seek closer ties with Minsk
"Commonwealth with Belarus is the common desire of our peoples and we will not deviate from this path," said Yeltsin, kissing Lukashenko on the cheek.
Russia and Belarus have formed a close two-way community inside the loose post-Soviet Commowealth of Independent States. The two leaders have committed themselves to achieving further integration.

Yeltsin said in his state of the nation address, presented to parliament on Thursday, that re-integration with Belarus was a foreign policy priority for Russia. But he said the process should not be artificially accelerated.
